preserved_prior_findings.external_crash_window_impossibility: Repository checkpoint ordering/readback alone cannot distinguish no-accept from accept-no-ack histories after a crash; retry risks duplicate and suppress risks omission.

minimal_external_effect_contract.G: Stable generation-scoped request identity k(g), distinct across generations and bound to the intended payload digest; conflicting payload under the same key is rejected.
minimal_external_effect_contract.I: Acceptance is idempotent with respect to k(g); same-generation replays create at most one logical external effect and preserve the same logical result.
minimal_external_effect_contract.V: Recovery has authoritative generation- and payload-correlated visibility of committed effect state/result, or an equivalent atomic coupling whose replay semantics supply that authority.

No public source, target call, external effect, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, shared ledger, legacy research, protected/manual execution, hosted compute, finite quota, or scheduler mutation.

verifier_predicates.P1_same_generation_key_stability: All retries for generation g use the same durable k(g).
verifier_predicates.P2_cross_generation_separation: For g1!=g2, keys cannot alias or be intentionally recycled within the correctness horizon.
verifier_predicates.P3_payload_binding: k(g) is bound to payload digest d(g); a different payload under the same key is rejected before a second effect can occur.
verifier_predicates.P4_idempotent_acceptance: Repeated submissions with the same valid k(g),d(g) yield at most one logical visible effect and a stable logical result.
verifier_predicates.P5_authoritative_visibility: Recovery can resolve k(g),d(g) against the authority that governs the visible effect, not merely a local checkpoint or best-effort cache.
verifier_predicates.P6_safe_noncommit_semantics: A not-committed/pending observation cannot falsely certify permanent nonacceptance while an earlier request may still commit; retry safety is supplied by P4.
verifier_predicates.P7_commit_gated_advancement: The Chat-local workflow advances past the effect only from authoritative committed/result evidence for the same k(g),d(g).
verifier_predicates.P8_generation_correlated_replay: A result or replay for an older generation cannot satisfy, suppress, or advance the current generation.

matrix.trace: Persist k(g),d(g); submit; effect commits; acknowledgment is lost; recovery queries authoritative V for k(g),d(g) and observes committed(result=r); any replay of the same key returns/preserves r; advance only on that committed evidence.
matrix.reason: Lost acknowledgment does not create duplication or omission and committed state is recoverably decidable.

matrix.trace: Effect may commit and acknowledgment is lost; replay is deduplicated but no authoritative committed-state/result observation exists.
matrix.reason: At-most-once may hold, but completion cannot be safely certified; advance risks false completion and never-advance violates recoverable progress.

matrix.trace: Attempt A is in flight; crash; recovery observes not-committed before A commits; retry B is issued; A and B both later commit.
matrix.reason: Visibility alone cannot fence a delayed original request from racing the retry, so duplicate visible effects remain possible.

matrix.trace: g1 commits under key k; g2 later reuses/aliases k; the endpoint suppresses g2 as duplicate or returns g1's result.
matrix.reason: A legitimate later generation can be omitted or misattributed even though per-key dedupe and visibility work.

matrix.trace: First submission uses k(g),d1; a later conflicting submission presents the same k(g) with d2!=d1.
matrix.expected: PASS only if hard-rejected before any second effect and V remains bound to d1; otherwise REJECT
matrix.reason: Stable keys without payload binding can convert accidental key reuse or mutation into wrong-result replay or duplicate side effects.

matrix.trace: Effect commits, but recovery visibility continues to report not-committed or cannot distinguish cache lag from true nonacceptance; retries are deduplicated.
matrix.reason: Idempotence prevents duplication, but stale visibility cannot provide recoverably decidable completion or safe commit-gated advancement.

matrix.clauses: broken G and/or broken generation correlation in V
matrix.trace: g1 commits under k; after apparent retirement or retention expiry, a later generation reuses k; stale committed state/result for g1 is observed during recovery of the later generation.
matrix.reason: A stale prior-generation commit can be mistaken for the current effect or suppress it unless identity is nonaliasing over the correctness horizon and visibility is generation/payload correlated.

matrix.trace: While generation g is active, a delayed replay/query for g-1 arrives. It may return the g-1 result but cannot mutate, satisfy, suppress, or advance g because k(g-1)!=k(g) and V is correlated to each generation/payload.
matrix.reason: This is the positive control that distinguishes harmless stale replay from ABA aliasing.

bounded_leaf_result.decision_rule: A candidate primitive satisfies the abstract crash-window contract only if M0, M4 and M7 meet their positive conditions and every adversarial M1, M2, M3, M5 and M6 is structurally prevented or rejected by the primitive's own semantics. Local repository checkpoint evidence alone cannot substitute for P5.
bounded_leaf_result.coverage_claim: Within this finite model, the matrix independently exercises lost-ack ambiguity, delayed-original races, generation aliasing, payload/key conflict, stale visibility, ABA/reuse, and stale replay isolation. It is a verifier specification, not evidence that any concrete Chat-capable primitive satisfies it.
bounded_leaf_result.exact_missing_capability: One concrete Chat-capable, zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, zero-incremental-cost external-effect primitive whose documented and testable semantics satisfy all positive conditions and structurally reject all adversarial rows in this matrix.
bounded_leaf_result.residual_dependency_classification: unresolved_child_capability; no richer-mode/protected/manual execution handoff is accepted
